add_block.new_heading: What the Arabic dish names mean
new_paragraphs: Dish names are the part hosts get stuck on when they compare two quotes, because a menu can list twenty words and explain none of them. Here is the plain-English version of the ones that come up most on a Dubai spread.
Hummus — chickpeas blended smooth with tahini, lemon and garlic.
Moutabal — aubergine roasted over flame until it tastes of smoke, then whipped with tahini and yoghurt. Baba ghanouj is its chunkier, salad-like cousin.
Tabbouleh — a parsley salad, not a bulgur one: chopped parsley and mint with a little cracked wheat, tomato, lemon and olive oil.
Fattoush — chopped garden salad with toasted or fried flatbread through it and sumac over the top.
Labneh — yoghurt strained until it is thick enough to scoop, served with olive oil and often mint or garlic.
Kibbeh — a shell of bulgur and minced meat stuffed with spiced meat and pine nuts, then fried; also baked in a tray as kibbeh bel saynieh.
Sambousek — small filled pastries, meat, cheese or spinach, baked or fried.
Manakish — flatbread baked to order with zaatar, cheese or minced meat. Breakfast food that works all day.
Mashawi — the charcoal grill section as a whole: skewers, chops and kofta cooked over coals.
Shish taouk — chicken marinated in garlic, lemon and yoghurt, grilled on skewers.
Kafta — minced lamb or beef worked with onion and parsley, moulded onto a skewer and grilled.
Kabsa — the Gulf rice dish: long-grain rice cooked with chicken or lamb, tomato and a warm spice mix.
Machboos — the Emirati and Khaleeji take on that rice, sharpened with loomi, the dried black lime.
Mandi — Yemeni in origin, meat and rice cooked low and slow so the smoke gets into the grain.
Makloubeh — “upside down”: rice layered with aubergine and meat in one pot, then flipped onto the platter to serve.
Mansaf — Jordanian lamb cooked in jameed, a tart dried yoghurt, poured over rice and thin bread.
Ouzi — the centrepiece: a whole slow-roasted lamb over spiced rice, carried in and carved at the table.
Kunafa — shredded pastry or fine semolina baked over melting cheese and soaked in sugar syrup, eaten hot.
Baklava — layered filo with nuts and syrup, cut into small pieces.
Umm Ali — Egyptian pudding of pastry baked in sweetened milk with nuts and raisins.
If you searched for arabic food names in dubai and landed here, that list is the vocabulary; the menu below is the whole range we design from.

add_block.new_heading: The full Arabic catering menu, course by course
new_paragraphs: The list above is the headline. Below is the whole menu we design from, set out in the order an Arabic spread is served: cold mezze first, then hot mezze and bakery, then the charcoal grill, then the rice and stew mains, then the centrepiece, then sweets. Nobody orders all of it. A menu is assembled section by section, and most hosts settle on five to eight cold mezze, three to five hot mezze, three to five items off the grill, three mains and three desserts. Most Dubai catering companies publish a dish list and stop there, but it is the section counts that let you compare two quotes honestly. And if you arrived searching for arabic food names in dubai, these are the real names, spelled the way a Levantine kitchen writes them.
Cold mezze — the opening spread
The largest section on any Arabic menu, and the one the table gets judged on. It goes down before guests sit and stays there all night.
Dips and purées: Hummus (vegan) · Moutabal (vegan) · Baba Ghanouj (vegan) · Mohamara · Beetroot Boutabal · Pesto Hummus · Sundried Tomato Hummus · Labneh with Garlic
Salads: Tabouleh · Fatoush (vegan) · Rocca Salad · Oriental Salad (vegan) · Lentil Tabouleh · Quinoa Tabouleh · Freekeh Salad · Beetroot Salad · Kale & Quinoa · Olive Salad
Cooked and preserved: Stuffed Vine Leaves (vegan) · Hindbeh · Eggplant Mousakaa · Makdous
Cheese board: Shanklish · Cheese with Thyme · Assorted Cheese
Crossovers Dubai hosts ask for: Caprese · Caesar Salad · Pasta Salad · Crab Salad — not Levantine, but they turn up on most Dubai Arabic buffets, so we list them instead of pretending otherwise

The strongest Arabic menus in Dubai publish around twenty-one cold appetisers and let you pick five, six or eight by package tier. That is the norm we hold to: eighteen to twenty-two listed, five to eight on your table.
Hot mezze — the pastries and the fryer
The second wave, sent out warm while the grill gets going.
Baked pastry: Sambousik Meat · Cheese Sambousik · Fatayer Spinach · Meat Sfiha · Cheese, Meat or Spinach Fatayer · Mini Chicken Moussakhan Roll
From the fryer: Fried Kebbe · Spiced Potato · Fried Chicken Liver · Fried Makanek · Fried Sujouk · Calamari, fried or provençal
Warm bowls: Foul · Hummus Balila · Fatteh with Yogurt
Skewers and rolls: Mini Lamb Kebab Skewers · Mini Shish Taouk Brochette · Mini Falafel Wrap (vegan) · Mini Labneh Roll with Mint
Manakish, saj and the Arabic bakery
Bread is a course here, not a basket on the side.
Manakish: Zaatar Manakish · Cheese Manakish · Kishek Manakish · Halloumi · Spinach pastry · Muhamara pastry · Labneh tartines
Lahem bajine, by home town: Lahem Beajine · Lahem Bajine Baalbaki · Lahem Bajine Traboulsi — three genuinely different breads, not three spellings of one
Saj toppings if the dome comes: zaatar, labneh, cheese, meat, turkey and cheese, with mint, tomato, cucumber, olives and spring onions alongside
Mashawi — the charcoal grill
Its own section on a proper Arabic menu, not folded into the mains.
Chicken and meat: Shish Tawouk · Grilled Meat · Kafta · Chicken Kafta · Arayess Kafta · Lamb Chops · Lamb Cubes · Makanek · Sujouk · Traditional Mix Grill
From the sea and the garden: Grilled Shrimp · Grilled Prawns · Grilled Fish Fillet · Grilled Vegetables

A charcoal mangal is an open-flame setup. Plenty of Dubai venues — rooftops, hotel terraces, yachts and most tower podiums — do not permit open charcoal, so we check it with your venue before it goes into the quote, not after. Where charcoal is not allowed, the same skewers come off gas or a flat-top and the menu does not change.
Mains — the rice and stew families
This is where a real Arabic caterer separates itself. The rice dishes are nine distinct things, not one dish called “Arabic rice with meat&rdquo.

Rice: Chicken Kabsah · Lamb Kabseh · Fish Kabseh · Chicken Mandi · Lamb Mansaf · Chicken Makloubeh · Lamb Makloubeh Eggplant · Chicken Freekeh · Chicken Moghrabieh · Oriental Chicken with Oriental Rice · Chicken Biryani · Meat Biryani
Kebbeh and kafta trays: Kebbeh Bel Laban · Kebbeh Bel Saynieh · Kafta Bel Saynieh

Stews: Dawood Basha with Rice · Shakrieh with Rice · Fasoulia Bel Lahmeh · Loubieh Bel Lahmeh · Bamieh Bel Lahmeh · Bazella Bel Lahmeh · Artichoke Lamb Potato Stew · Chicken Mouloukhieh with Rice · Chicken Tagine
Mahshi — the stuffed dishes: Koussa Waraq Inab and Fawaergh · Koussa & Warak Enab Bel Lahmeh · Stuffed Koussa with Tomato Sauce · Mahshi Malfouf · Sheikh El Mehshi · Stuffed Vine Leaves with Meat
Chicken and fish: Chicken Mousakhan · Dajaj Al Faham · Dajaj Bel Saynieh with Lemon & Coriander Sauce · Fish Sayadieh · Samkeh Harra with Tahina or Tomato Sauce
Roasts and the one Spanish guest: Roast Lamb with Oriental Rice · Seafood Paella — the paella earns its place because it feeds a crowd from one pan and sits happily beside mezze
The centrepiece — ouzi and whole roasts
Quoted separately from the buffet, because it is a separate piece of work: an oven that takes a whole lamb, insulated hot transport, and a chef carving in front of your guests.
Lamb: Full Roasted Lamb Station · Lamb with Rice · Lamb with Freekeh · Lamb with Mansaf · Lamb with Warak Inab, Kousa & Fawaregh · Warak Inab, Kousa & Lamb Chops · Lamb Leg · Boneless Lamb
Other roasts: Roasted Chicken with Rice or Freekeh · Turkey · Beef Filet · Roasted Beef · Grilled Hammour
Sides: Stuffed Lamb · Stuffed Chicken · Mashed Potatoes & Veg

Most centrepieces come as a half or a full portion, and the grain bed is yours to choose: rice, freekeh, mansaf, or warak inab with kousa and fawaregh. As a rough sizing guide, a whole roast lamb carries a table of around thirty as the centre of a wider spread.
Live stations
An Arabic offering with fewer than four or five stations is a thin one. Stations are quoted as their own units with quantities attached, so you can see what you are buying.
Live Arabic BBQ: shish taouk, kafta kebab, lamb cubes, grilled prawns and grilled vegetables, with garlic paste
Live shawarma: a vertical spit, chicken or beef, with Arabic bread, fries, garlic paste, tomato, pickles and sliced lettuce. Chicken and beef run on separate spits
Live saj: a baker at the dome turning out zaatar, labneh and cheese manakish to order
Live falafel: fried on site and handed over with Arabic bread, tomato, parsley, pickles and tahina. Sized at 5 kg, which covers about thirty guests
Barbecue station: 10 kg across shish tawouk, grilled meat, kafta, arayess kafta and lamb chops, cooked over charcoal as guests come up
Full roasted lamb station: carved to order, and one whole lamb carries a table of around thirty
Mixed grill station: tawook, kabab and tikka skewers grilled in front of guests
Wagyu shawarma station: 10 kg on the spit, for when the shawarma is the headline rather than the filler
Cheese kunafa station: warm kunafa in copper trays, served in buns — a station is quoted with 100 buns
Knefeh & sweets station and the merry cream station for the end of the night
Anything with a live flame or hot oil depends on the venue giving power, extraction and permission. We confirm each of those with the venue before the station appears on your quote.
Arabic canapés and mini bites
How Levantine flavour is served standing up, at a corporate reception or a cocktail hour.
Kebbeh balls, stuffed with hommos, moutabal, beetroot hommos or tabbouleh and topped with pomegranate
Wraps and parcels: Labneh Wrap Sushi Style · Chicken Shawarma Moneybags · Mini Beef or Chicken Shawarma Wrap · Pita Pocket with vegetable, makanek or sujuk
Tartlets and shooters: Hummus Beetroot in Tartlet (vegan) · Mini Hummus & Roasted Pepper Phyllo Bites (vegan) · Vine Leaves Tzatziki in Shooters (vegan)
Halloumi and othmaliyeh: Halloumi Dippers with Pesto · Othmaliyeh halloumi with black olive tapenade and tomato jam · Shrimp Othmaliye · Chicken Mousakhan bite
Mini brioche sandwiches: Falafel · Makanek · Shawarma · Kofta · Feta & Zaatar · Halloumi with Zaatar · Labneh with Mint & Cucumber · Mini Falafel Sandwich (vegan)
Open face: Labneh and olives with fresh zaatar · Beetroot hommos with roasted zucchini (vegan)
Arabic breakfast, Iftar and Suhoor
Its own package, not a shortened dinner buffet. An iftar opens with dates and lentil soup before the mezze goes down.
Cold: Labneh Salad · Assorted Cheese · Olive Salad · Makdous · Assorted Jams
Hot: Foul · Hummus Balila · Fatteh with Yogurt · Eggs of your choice
Manakeesh: Zaatar · Cheese · Kishek · Lahem Beajine
To open the fast: Dates · Lentil soup (shorbat adas) · freshly baked Arabic breads
See Ramadan iftar and suhoor catering for the full seasonal build.
Arabic desserts
Warm, from the pan: Cheese Kunafa · Halawet El Jebben · Katayef Kashta · Othmalieh · Umm Ali · Awamat with Date Syrup · Luqaimat
Cold and spooned: Riz Bel Halib · Mohalabieh with Orange · Mouhalabieh with pistachio in a shooter glass · Custard · Crème Caramel
Trays and sweets: Baklava · Basboussa · Nammorra · Ghraybeh · Mafroukeh · Coated Chocolate Dates · Assorted Mini Cakes · Sliced fruit
Drinks
Fresh juices in orange, mango, strawberry, pineapple and lemon mint, alongside mineral water and soft drinks. Arabic tea and coffee come with the breakfast and iftar packages.
Vegan, vegetarian, gluten-free, dairy-free — and a straight word about nuts

Arabic is the easiest cuisine on this site to serve meat-free without building a second menu, and we tag it at dish level instead of burying it in a footnote. Hummus, moutabal, baba ghanouj, fattoush, tabbouleh, stuffed vine leaves, oriental salad, lentil salad, mini falafel wrap and fatayer are all vegan as written. For a wedding or a large reception we set up a standalone vegan and vegetarian counter instead of hiding the options inside the main buffet.

Two honest cautions. The mezze spread is bread-led, so a gluten-free path needs deliberate substitution and is not a matter of lifting the pita off the table — and labneh, shanklish, halloumi, kunafa and halawet el jebben are dairy-central, so a dairy-free guest needs their own line. Gluten-free options are available on request, subject to partner confirmation and an allergen review for the specific booking.

On nuts: no Arabic menu we read across the Dubai market discloses this, so we will. Baklava, ghraybeh, mafroukeh and mohamara are nut-heavy, and pine nuts garnish several of the rice and kebbeh dishes. Menus without intentionally added nuts may be available on request. However, partner kitchens may handle nuts and other allergens, so cross-contact cannot be excluded unless specifically confirmed.

Gluten-free, nut-conscious and other dietary menu options may be available on request, subject to confirmation by the assigned culinary partner. Partner kitchens may handle allergens, and cross-contact cannot be completely excluded unless dedicated controls have been specifically confirmed for the booking. Guests with allergies must provide full details before confirming their event. We will not describe a menu as free of an allergen unless the culinary partner responsible for cooking it confirms the required controls can be achieved.

new_paragraphs: Plenty of enquiries start as a search for an arabic restaurant dubai hosts can book out — a long table in Bur Dubai, a terrace at Dubai Creek Harbour, somewhere in Dubai Hills for twenty-five people on a Friday. The food is the reason, but the room rarely fits: restaurant private rooms cap out, the menu is fixed, and a majlis layout is not something a dining room can give you. Catering solves the same craving in the opposite direction — the mezze, the mashawi and the ouzi arrive where you already are, at whatever headcount you have. Nobody is asking you to name the top arabic restaurant dubai has and settle for its set menu.

The other thing a restaurant cannot do is mix cuisines across one event. MyCHEF arranges Italian catering in Dubai , Pakistani and North Indian menus, seafood and BBQ alongside the Levantine spread, so a three-day corporate programme or a wedding weekend can change character each night under one booking. See all cuisines .

Working or office lunch, dropped off: from AED 90 per person

new_paragraphs: How much does Arabic catering cost in Dubai?

It starts from AED 90 per person for a dropped-off spread, AED 120 for a standard buffet and AED 150 for a premium buffet with live stations. A staffed private chef, cooking and serving on site, is AED 700 to 950 per person. Minimums are 10 guests on volume formats, 20 on a full buffet, and AED 900 on order value, and we quote every element itemised.
What's included in Arabic catering?
Everything from menu planning and the chef to service staff, plating and cleanup. One team covers all of it, so you host and we run the event.
Is halal Arabic catering available?
Yes. Arabic menus can be prepared fully halal as standard; just confirm when you enquire, and see our dedicated halal catering page.
Do you cater Ramadan iftars and suhoors?
Yes, and it is one of our busiest seasons. We build generous iftar and suhoor spreads for family majlis, corporate gatherings and large events across the city.
Can you handle dietary requirements?
Yes. Vegetarian, vegan, gluten-free and nut-aware versions of most Arabic dishes are on the menu on request; share your guest list and we adjust accordingly.
How do I book Arabic catering?
Share your date, guest count and venue; we match a vetted chef and send an itemised proposal, usually within one business day.
How far in advance should I book?

As guidance: 72 hours for a standard Arabic catering package, 3–5 days where live stations or a multi-staff setup are involved, 5–7 days for bespoke menus and larger private events, and 7–14 days or more for weddings and corporate functions. We recommend booking as early as possible. Lead times depend on guest numbers, menu complexity, staffing, equipment, location and partner availability. Booking late for a arabic? Send the date first; whether it works depends on which partners are free.
For arabic catering, the chefs and partner kitchens handling your booking operate to Dubai Municipality food-safety requirements .
